summary: Lodash-impersonating obfuscated bundle exfiltrates browser wallet/password state via WebSocket
details: @finaxis/common-js@0.3.8 ships a single javascript-obfuscator-packed bundle at dist/common-js.js whose decoded string table contains 'wallet', 'password', 'localStorage', 'atob', 'AES', 'encrypt', 'decrypt', 'WebSocket', and 'fetch'. The package implements none of the lodash API but ships a verbatim copy of lodash's README and declares keywords ['lodash','lodash-js'] under the unrelated name @finaxis/common-js — a lodash brand-impersonation cover story. When loaded (via require/import or via the declared unpkg/jsdelivr entry in a browser context), the bundle reads browser-side secret material (wallet extension state, stored passwords, localStorage) and ships it to a remote endpoint over WebSocket and fetch, using AES to encrypt the outbound traffic and hide the destination. The persistent WebSocket also provides a bidirectional channel back into the page. package.json's scripts.obfuscate runs javascript-obfuscator over the plain source to produce the shipped bundle, confirming the concealment is deliberate.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
